items.title: GLM-5.3 opens a stronger coding model
items.oneliner: Z.ai open-sourced GLM-5.3 with a 50% code benchmark jump, raising the floor for self-hosted coding assistants.

items.title: Multi-agent systems are doing real math
items.oneliner: Researchers let agents roam an open environment and got 12 solved math problems plus proofs, not just polished demos.

items.title: Bug rumors now trigger exploit races
items.oneliner: Attackers probed cohttp within minutes of a patch hint, shrinking responsible disclosure into a near-zero-day window.

items.title: Agent security is becoming the real blocker
items.oneliner: The hard part is no longer model safety; it is tool access, permissions, and prompt injection across agent workflows.

items.title: AI copyright bots are causing takedowns
items.oneliner: Luanti got pulled from Google Play over a baseless Tracer.AI DMCA, showing automated enforcement can break legitimate software.

items.title: Smart TVs remain hostile home computers
items.oneliner: The warning is simple: firmware updates can become surveillance vectors, and consumer devices still ship with asymmetric control.

items.title: DRAM is starting to do inference math
items.oneliner: Samsung's LPDDR5X-PIM pushes 614 GB/s inside memory, attacking the bandwidth wall that throttles LLM inference.

items.title: htmx 4.0 modernizes its web plumbing
items.oneliner: htmx 4.0 moves toward fetch(), drops localStorage dependence, and makes inheritance explicit without breaking the old mental model.

items.title: scc 4.0 turns code counts into hotspots
items.oneliner: scc 4.0 combines complexity with change history, giving teams a faster way to find risky files before bugs do.

items.title: A judge rejected Anthropic's blacklisting
items.oneliner: A federal judge reportedly ruled Anthropic's government blacklisting illegal, reminding AI vendors that procurement fights are now strategic.
